narrative: 当你想让这句“话”听起来像是在“看”，而不是在“用镜头拍”时，就选50mm。脸保持着正常的比例。
房间既不会向前冲，也不会挤压进画面。对话、过肩镜头，还有普通的单人镜头都活在这个焦段里，因为观众不会被要求去注意到这支镜头本身的存在。
当空间本身必须“发表意见”时，这不是合适的工具。24mm会让房间成为一个搭档。
85mm则会把人变成一片风景。在同一个三脚架位置上，换成50mm只是改变了裁切范围；如果你想要压缩感，依然需要退后，然后用更长焦的镜头。
how: 先站在人类对话的常见距离上。在大致相当于35mm规格的传感器上，50mm是一个温和的中长焦“标准”镜头；在全画幅上，它则是经典的静态摄影标准镜头。
无论哪种情况，都让节点保持在一个正常人会站的位置，让视野自然呈现。除非光圈开得很大，或者靠得很近，否则50mm的景深是中等程度的。
提示词：50mm normal lens on [Subject], human-scale perspective, neither compressed nor stretched, conversational truth.
when: 当你不想让镜头本身“发表意见”时使用它：隔着桌子的谈话、一个应该显得像被观察、而不是被刻意塑造的单人镜头。不要用它在固定站位上假冒长焦式的孤立感，或者广角式的环境拉伸。
vs: 35mm中广角在同一站位上展示更多一点的世界；85mm人像镜头需要更远的站位，并开始压缩背景。
球面镜头（Spherical）说的是镜头的光学结构；50mm通常是球面镜头，但“球面”本身不是一个焦距。近距离拍摄的24mm广角则是关于空间的另一句完全不同的话。
examples_film: 经典的覆盖镜头体系常常把50mm用在单人镜头和过肩镜头上，让镜头本身“消失”，让表演和调度来承载整场戏。把它当作一种语法来借鉴：对话式的距离、真实的比例，没有堆叠压缩的城市，也没有逼近突兀的家具。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的近邻是被误标为“标准”的35mm中广角，或者85mm人像镜头——因为生成模型往往把每一张脸都当成人像焦段来处理。破绽是多出来的房间信息（35mm），或者一片被冲淡、堆叠的背景（85mm）。
解决办法：站在对话距离上，保持完整的面部比例，让背景存在，但不显得拥挤。

faq.a: 这是传统意义上的标准焦距：在一个典型的站位上，既不拉伸近处物体，也不压缩远处平面。透视依然取决于你把摄影机放在哪里。
50mm在对话距离上保持房间的真实感，脸也不会被堆叠。85mm从更远的地方拍摄，放大背景、削薄景深、制造孤立感。50mm是对话，85mm是把脸当作风景。
当镜头本身应该“消失”时使用它：对话、见证、普通的覆盖镜头。当空间必须拉伸、堆叠，或者制造孤立感时跳过它。

faq.q: How do I prompt 50mm normal for AI image or video?
faq.a: 写：50mm normal lens on [Subject], human-scale perspective, neither compressed nor stretched, conversational truth。点名一个对话距离。禁止超广角式的拉伸和长焦式的堆叠。

narrative: A 50mm is the length you pick when the sentence should sound like looking, not like a lens. Faces keep proportion.
Rooms neither rush forward nor crowd in. Conversations, over-the-shoulders, and plain singles live here because the audience is not asked to notice the optic.
It is the wrong tool when space itself must argue. A 24mm will make the room a partner.
An 85mm will make the person a landscape. From the same tripod, switching to 50mm only crops; if you wanted compression you still have to walk back, then use longer glass.
how: Stand first at a human talking distance. On a roughly 35mm-wide sensor, 50mm is a mild tele-normal; on full frame it is the classic still-camera normal.
Either way, keep the nodal point where a person would stand, and let the field fall out. Depth of field at 50mm is moderate unless you open very wide or get close.
Prompt: 50mm normal lens on [Subject], human-scale perspective, neither compressed nor stretched, conversational truth.
when: Use it when you do not want the glass to editorialize: a talk across a table, a single that should feel observed rather than styled. Do not use it to fake telephoto isolation or wide environmental stretch from a fixed stand.
vs: 35mm Moderate Wide shows a little more world from the same stand. 85mm Portrait requires a farther stand and starts to compress the background.
Spherical is the lens construction; a 50mm is usually spherical, but spherical is not a focal length. 24mm Wide from close is a different sentence about space.
examples_film: Classical coverage often parks the 50mm on singles and over-the-shoulders so the optic disappears and performance plus blocking carry the scene. Use that as grammar: conversational distance, honest proportion, no stacked city and no looming furniture.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is 35mm Moderate Wide labeled as normal, or 85mm Portrait because generators treat every face as a portrait length. The tell is extra room (35) or a washed, stacked background (85).
Fix: talking-distance stand, full-face proportion, background present but not crowding.

faq.a: It is the conventional normal focal length: a field that neither stretches near objects nor compresses distant planes from a typical stand. Perspective still comes from where you put the camera.

50mm at talking distance keeps the room honest and the face unstacked. 85mm from farther back enlarges the background, thins depth of field, and isolates. 50mm is conversation. 85mm is the face as landscape.
Use it when the optic should disappear: talk, witness, plain coverage. Skip it when space must stretch, stack, or isolate.

faq.q: How do I prompt 50mm normal for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: 50mm normal lens on [Subject], human-scale perspective, neither compressed nor stretched, conversational truth. Name a talking distance. Forbid ultra-wide stretch and telephoto stack.
